clue.text: She wrote 18 dn

parts.note: 18 down is a word meaning in metre, so the clue describes a woman who wrote her works in verse

explanation.surface: A woman is credited with writing another entry in this very puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the whole trick: 18 down reads IN VERSE, so 'she wrote in verse' describes a female writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who composes verse is a female poet, an old-fashioned title for such a writer.

clue.text: An off-hand forecaster

parts.note: off-hand normally means casual, but here it means one who tells the future from the hand

explanation.surface: Someone who makes casual, offhand predictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-hand' looks like 'casual'; read literally, the forecast comes off the hand, from its lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller who reads the lines on a person's hand predicts what lies ahead.

clue.text: Unusual crest seen in .the upright position

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of crest and seen appear in an out-of-the-ordinary order

explanation.surface: A strange crest is spotted standing straight up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges CREST and SEEN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing straight up is the state of being vertical, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: Bearing on the water-supply in Surrey

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the bearing comes first

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
a well supplies water

explanation.surface: A compass direction fixed on the water source in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Ewell is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London; 'in Surrey' defines it as a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewell is a town near Epsom, in that county south of London.

clue.text: Old fellow responsible for impasse

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: An elderly man is to blame for a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken from chess, the word means a position in which no further progress is possible: a deadlock.

clue.text: Fitting accommodation for electrical equipment

parts.note: read as housing provided for gear, the phrase really means the wall fittings that receive electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Somewhere suitable to house some electrical gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like the adjective 'suitable', but it is the noun: these are fittings that accommodate plugs and bulbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall outlets and lampholders are the fixtures into which plugs and bulbs are fitted.

clue.text: View a lot

definitions.meaning: a view or spectacle, something seen
informally 'a ...' means a great deal, as in 'a ... better'

explanation.surface: A scene with plenty in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle you look at is a view, and colloquially 'a sight more' means a great deal more.

clue.text: Study to catch up with the German rival

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for catch is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to net is to catch
der is German for 'the'

explanation.surface: A student cramming to draw level with a German competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NET to TEN in this down clue; 'to' and 'with' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor contending for a prize or title is a rival to the others.

clue.text: Survive, though no longer first

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
1st, written with I for 1, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone stays alive even though they are not at the front any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, with the numeral read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on living or being is to survive, to have being at all.

clue.text: He may be waiting for a train

definitions.text: He may be waiting for a train

parts.words: He may be waiting for a train
parts.note: it suggests a passenger on a platform, but waiting means serving at table, in a railway dining car

explanation.surface: A man standing on a platform expecting his train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiting for' looks like expecting; it means serving, as a waiter does, on board a train.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who serves food and drink to passengers on a ship, plane or train has this title.

clue.text: Vassal spreading a malicious story around for example

parts.note: a lie is a false and malicious story

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the abbreviation for 'for example' back to front

explanation.surface: A feudal underling is putting about a spiteful falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' only links; a 'malicious story' is simply a falsehood, and 'Vassal' is the less familiar sense of a word usually meaning a feudal lord.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal usage the word could denote either the lord or the subject owing him allegiance, here the latter.

clue.text: Entering a developing country

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters of the words before it are still taking a new form

explanation.surface: Going into a nation that is still developing economically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' looks like it describes the country, but it is the anagram signal for the letters of ENTERING and A.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The Argentine' is an older name for the South American republic Argentina.

clue.text: "Go! put off Holiness, and put on" (Blake)

definitions.text: "Go! put off Holiness, and put on" (Blake)

parts.words: "Go! put off Holiness, and put on" (Blake)
parts.note: the solver completes a line from William Blake's poetry, which urges casting aside piety in favour of the reasoning mind

explanation.surface: A line of William Blake's verse with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the line from Blake reads 'Go! put off Holiness, and put on Intellect'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the faculty of reason, which Blake sets against holiness in this line.

clue.text: Making some pretext, radioed for more

indicators.note: Making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone invents an excuse and sends it over the airwaves, asking for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making some' tells you to take part of the words that follow: the letters sit across 'pretEXT, RAdioed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is what you get when you ask for more, so 'for more' stands for an added amount.

clue.text: A step on the stairs

parts.note: this looks like one footfall taken on a staircase, but it names the horizontal board of each stair that the foot rests on

explanation.surface: Someone takes one step on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase, the horizontal board you put your foot on is called this, as opposed to the riser.

clue.text: Record concerning daughter — it will bring shame

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A daughter's record will bring the family into disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the plain word IT; 'will bring' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgrace someone or damage their reputation is to shame them.

clue.text: Left a group of musicians done in

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: 'done in' means wrecked, so the word done is broken up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A band of musicians departed, completely exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' looks like 'exhausted', but 'in' is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'done', after A and BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind and deserted is described as forsaken.

clue.text: An admonition concerning hors d'oeuvres

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice or warning, an admonition
'as to' means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A warning given about the starters at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' is 'as to', two words that supply the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for starters served before the main course of a meal.

clue.text: Exotic fruit — several found lying around smashed crate

indicators.note: lying around means the number word surrounds the remaining letters

parts.note: nine stands for several, an indefinite number

indicators.note: smashed suggests the crate is broken and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Imported fruit discovered strewn around a broken packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges the letters of 'crate', and 'lying around' puts the number word around them; 'found' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach, once thought of as a foreign delicacy.

clue.text: Playing tennis — it's demanding

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of tennis and it's are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a game of tennis is a demanding business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges the letters of TENNIS and IT'S; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone demanding keeps pressing a point and will not let it drop, which is persistence.

clue.text: Metrically rendered or quite the opposite

definitions.meaning: written in metre, as a poem
the reverse or contrary of something

explanation.surface: Something is either put into verse or turned completely on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means written as poetry; as one word it means the contrary or reverse.

clue.text: Note a dog's come round again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cur is a mongrel dog; the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A remark that a dog has come back round once more.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is a note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi).
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps happening again and again comes round once more.

clue.text: The raw beginner infuriates the older guides

indicators.note: beginner means the opening letter of the word raw is taken

parts.note: angers means infuriates

explanation.surface: An inexperienced newcomer annoys the senior tour leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers were the senior section of the Girl Guides, for older girls.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior branch of the Girl Guide movement, for older members, was known by this name.

clue.text: Face-saving device that may prevent a glare

definitions.text: Face-saving device that may prevent a glare

parts.words: Face-saving device that may prevent a glare
parts.note: face-saving usually means avoiding embarrassment, but here it is literal: a shield for the face that also shades the eyes

explanation.surface: A tactic to avoid humiliation that might head off an angry stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face-saving' and 'glare' suggest embarrassment and a hostile look; really it is a helmet's face guard or a cap's brim that shades from bright light.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet's movable front piece or a cap's peak protects the face and shades the eyes from strong light.

clue.text: Lip 'dressing

definitions.meaning: lip is cheek or impudent talk

explanation.surface: Something to apply to the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent talk is lip or cheek, and a liquid poured over food is a dressing.

clue.text: Refer to a page with audacious -article in

parts.note: pert means cheeky or audacious
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Consult a page that contains a cheeky piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; 'in' is the plain word IN, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain to something is to relate or belong to it, just as one matter may refer to another.

clue.text: Pole in space preparing lists

indicators.note: in tells us the pole goes inside the word for space

parts.note: an area is a space
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A polar explorer in outer space is getting ready to make lists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' is the old word for a jousting ground, not inventories; 'preparing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The lists were the enclosed ground for medieval jousting, a place of contest.

clue.text: Quickly made .right with a well-turned bon-mot

indicators.note: well-turned here means the word for a witticism is turned back to front

parts.note: a pun is a witty remark, a bon mot

explanation.surface: Someone is quick to put things right with an elegant witticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-turned' looks like praise for the phrasing; it reverses PUN to NUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a garment or a structure is to make it hastily.

clue.text: Plump appearance' of sons under-worked

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or manipulated, so the letters of sons and under are reshaped

explanation.surface: A man's sons look chubby because they are not given enough work.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'under-worked' is split: its first part joins 'sons' as letters to rearrange, and 'worked' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chubby, rounded look is the quality of being circular in shape, applied to a figure.

clue.text: A sound description!

parts.note: 'sound' here is not 'reliable' but audio: a word that describes any sound at all

explanation.surface: Praise for a well-judged account of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like the adjective meaning reliable; it is the noun, and the answer is a general word for any sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Any audible disturbance, from a clatter to a din, can be described with this general word.

clue.text: A-Greek heroine's picked soldiers

parts.note: elect means chosen or picked
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of British soldiers

explanation.surface: A heroine of Greek legend has a hand-picked military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a stock crossword source of soldiers; the 's stands for 'has' and links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy she is Agamemnon's daughter, who helps avenge her father's murder.

clue.text: Underworld visitor pulling strings

parts.note: it suggests a gangster using influence, but means the mythical musician who went down to Hades and played the lyre

explanation.surface: A gangland figure manipulating events behind the scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' and 'pulling strings' suggest organised crime; in myth this lyre-player went down to Hades to fetch back Eurydice.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Thracian bard descended to Hades and charmed its rulers with his lyre playing.
